action: Analyzed closeout (650 lines) and shipit (680 lines) for bloat. Identified: onboarding prose, unimplemented features, redundant examples, duplicate sections. Estimated 78% reduction possible.
thinking: User asked if closeout/shipit could be optimized. Read both files and categorized every section as essential behavioral instruction vs verbose reference material. Found ~53% of each file was non-essential at invocation time.
decisions: Primary files carry behavioral instructions only
Secondary reference files for on-demand content
insights: Skills already use subfolder structure that supports secondary files
Unimplemented/deferred features were burning tokens every invocation

action: Rewrote both files. closeout: 650→137 lines (-77%). shipit: 680→113 lines (-79%). Created wai-closeout-reference.md for moved content.
thinking: Preserved every step and behavioral rule while removing: 4 use cases, Step 0 (deferred idempotency), Step 9d (no health-check.jsonl), Step 12 (deferred summary), all JSON examples, all report templates, language rules, duplicate success criteria. Shipit: removed use cases, Step 5c (no tests), Step 10 (duplicates closeout 9b), output format template.
decisions: Reference file only created when cut content has value
insights: Skill Thrift should apply to ALL skills
open: 31 remaining skills need the same treatment
evolution: Principle proven on two heaviest skills — ready for systematic rollout

action: Created epic-skill-thrift-v1 with tiered plan. Tier 1: 9 skills >200 lines, Tier 2: 6 skills 100-200 lines, Tier 3: 16 skills <100 lines (review only).
thinking: User wants to closeout and continue in fresh session. Created actionable epic with per-skill process and verification criteria so any agent can pick this up cold.
decisions: Tier 3 likely already lean — review pass only
insights: Estimated total savings: 25K+ tokens across all skills
evolution: Epic captures full plan for next session
